Discordant

/dis-KOR-dnt/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Discordant means not in harmony or agreement; clashing or jarring.

During warm-up, a single out-of-tune violin produced a discordant whine that cut through the orchestra's careful tuning.

Worked Example

At the reunion, the conversation about where to hold next year's gathering quickly turned discordant. Three aunts wanted the lake house, two cousins insisted on the city, and no two voices seemed to agree on anything.

The family's clashing, conflicting opinions show that discordant describes disagreement between people, not only harsh sound.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

clashing: conflicting sharply with something else

jarring: harsh, unsettling, out of place

inharmonious: lacking harmony or pleasing combination

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

harmonious: combining in a pleasing, agreeable way

compatible: able to exist together without conflict

Where it sits · how harshly things grate together — mismatched → discordant → cacophonous

mismatched vs. discordant: Mismatched things merely fail to go together, while discordant things actively clash or grate against each other.

cacophonous vs. discordant: A discordant sound clashes with what surrounds it, but a cacophonous one is a full, deafening jumble of harsh noise.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dis-

Prefix — dis-: apart

Root — cord

Root — cord: heart (Latin cor, cordis)

Suffix — -ant

Suffix — -ant: being in a state of (adjective-forming)

Put it together

Put it together: Discordant combines dis-, here meaning apart, with the Latin root cor, cordis, meaning heart, plus the adjective ending -ant, so it literally describes hearts apart, not agreeing. The same heart root appears in cordial, concord, and courage.

Use the root in a new word: concord

Use the root in a new word: concord: After decades of rivalry, the two towns finally lived in concord, even sharing a summer festival.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral / descriptive

Discordant is an adjective; it describes a note, a color scheme, or a relationship that clashes. Its related noun, dissonance, names the lack of harmony itself and is taught separately in this unit, so keep discordant for describing things: a discordant chord, a discordant meeting.
